title: Is the two-generator Burnside group of exponent 5 finite?
credit: Classical (open since the 1930s/1970s); listed in Kourovka notebook and standard surveys
premise_risks: Sub-question of the person-named Burnside problem; it is the specific unnamed instance 'Is B(2,5) finite?', allowed under the sub-question rule
plain: Take the 'freest' group generated by two elements a and b in which every element g satisfies g^5 = 1. Is this group finite? For exponents 2, 3, 4 and 6 the answer is yes; for large exponents it is infinite; exponent 5 with two generators is the smallest case nobody can decide. If it is finite, it must have exactly 5^34 elements.
math: Let $F_2$ be the free group on $\{a,b\}$ and $N=\langle\!\langle g^5: g\in F_2\rangle\!\rangle$. Decide whether $B(2,5)=F_2/N$ is finite. (Equivalently, since its largest finite quotient $R(2,5)$ has order $5^{34}$ by Havas-Wall-Wamsley and Kostrikin: decide whether $|B(2,5)|=5^{34}$.)
